#3054. Nvidia’s Earnings Call Is the AI Economy’s Next Stress Test

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Jensen Huang's departure was only a symptom of a bigger problem.

Nvidia’s shaky future in the wake of the departure of scandal-plagued founder and CEO Jensen Huang might get clearer Tuesday as the company reports quarterly earnings. If the company at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom can’t reassure investors, it could pull the whole industry into the muck with it.

The chipmaker’s stock price has already plunged 35% from last month’s high, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market cap and triggering Wall Street panic around a broader AI reckoning.

In the lead-up to the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Huang issued a statement that he would return as CEO if the board of directors decides it’s in the “best interest” of shareholders and the country. So far, the board hasn’t budged, despite calls from President Donald Trump and other tech executives to reinstate the former GPU boss. The Securities and Exchange Commission is also investigating Nvidia over concerns that the company misled investors, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Nvidia’s finance chief and interim CEO, Colette Kress, is now tasked with convincing investors that the semiconductor giant is moving in a stable direction and appeasing fears about potential national security violations amid illegal export deals. Market confidence is also shaky amid supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers that remain critical to AI compute and the training of large language models.

Huang maneuvered Nvidia into a linchpin role for frontier AI labs and data center firms, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing equity, credit and financial backing and by mobilizing third-party capital to secure investment for the AI buildout of data centers. Nvidia’s circular financing schemes — in which the chipmaker helps fund a hyperscaler like Meta or Microsoft, which then uses the funds to buy its products — were allegedly a source of contention for Kress and other executives. Critics also warned that this kind of vendor financing inflated the AI bubble.

According to Reuters, Kress may pull back from some of the riskiest AI financial deals, including investments in OpenAI and AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda. Already, Nvidia has significantly scaled back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal. During Tuesday’s call, Kress could lay out how the company plans to handle other outstanding deals inked by Huang, especially since Nvidia can no longer rely on a big chunk of revenue from under-the-table exports.

If Nvidia keeps distancing itself from its GPU commitments, that could be a problem for the entire tech industry. Semiconductor production is an incredibly specialized field dominated by very few companies, and any changes to the supply chain could have ripple effects on global markets and vendors, including in consumer electronics and cloud services.

Nvidia supplies the lion’s share of the hardware necessary for data center construction and model training, and the company has long said that the demand for chips exceeds supply. Shortages of RAM and high-bandwidth memory slow down the production of AI servers and raise prices for cloud companies and other buyers. In an attempt to buy its way out of the bottleneck, Nvidia has committed large sums of money to secure future memory supply.

But Huang’s affair with a Chinese executive connected to the Singapore-based Megaspeed — whom US intelligence claimed was a Chinese intelligence asset — complicated an already tight supply chain. Megaspeed was under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms obtain high-value Nvidia chips through channels that violated US export controls.

According to the investment research firm Culper, up to one-fifth of Nvidia’s fiscal-year 2026 compute revenues were driven by movement of some of the company’s most advanced chips into China through nonrestricted intermediary countries in a process called diversion. When advanced Nvidia chips or servers are illegally routed to Chinese buyers, those units are no longer available to legal customers in the US and allied markets.

Huang was influential in shaping the Trump administration’s chip export policies, pushing back against export controls that limited Nvidia’s sales to China. But the recent scandal prompted new Commerce Department restrictions on chip shipments through third countries. Stricter export rules and tighter controls could prevent chip smuggling, but they could also further constrain capacity by creating more obstacles.

Any company that supplies essential hardware for the AI buildout is at risk if investor confidence in the industry falters. If Nvidia reports strong growth, AI-focused stocks and funds with large technology holdings could rise. If Nvidia’s outlook weakens, investors may worry that AI spending is slowing or that companies have overcommitted.

A handful of big tech companies — colloquially known as the Magnificent Seven — make up a big share of major funds and indices. Five of them account for roughly 30% of the S&P 500 index, and AI overexposure in those businesses translates into overexposure in many individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Because index funds hold substantial positions in Nvidia and other large tech companies, an AI selloff could affect retirement balances even for people who don’t own Nvidia shares directly.

While the biggest AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic haven’t gone public (yet), the Magnificent Seven are heavily affected by AI stock swings. Alphabet’s stock price sank as Nvidia news aftershocks reverberated through the markets, proving that top firms are not unassailable. Other tech companies heavily focused on AI infrastructure, such as Intel and CoreWeave, likewise saw their share prices decline.

Amid growing concerns over AI dangers, Huang was one of AI’s most aggressive promoters, framing the technology as an economic and national-security imperative. In early September, the now-disgraced CEO said that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, had arrived, congratulating OpenAI on its GPT-6 Astra model, which was trained on Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell GPUs.

Huang pushed against recent warnings from AI researchers, calling for unrestrained progress on frontier models and repeatedly arguing against new laws and safety regulations.

Even before Huang’s business and personal scandals came to light, AI companies were gearing up for a post-midterm-election PR campaign, as the technology has become increasingly unpopular and the backlash against data centers has grown. Democratic Party politicians pushed a platform to shift the federal government’s lax approach toward the AI industry. Some Democrats are also poised to craft legislation to prevent an AI industry bailout in the event of a bubble pop.

Amid bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress, many politicians are also seeking to investigate high-ranking members of US intelligence and the Commerce Department for allowing export loopholes or for failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia’s China-related deals.

Kress might be able to lead Nvidia with tact and diligence, separating the company from some of its riskiest deals. But the national security implications of her predecessor’s relationships have opened up a can of worms that no CEO can close on their own.

The federal government is ruled by inertia, but right now there’s some investigative momentum aimed directly at the major AI players. That will almost certainly ice out some investor hype. Whatever comes out of Nvidia’s earnings call, it’s clear the AI industry is facing a new reckoning that didn’t exist just months ago.

#3053. Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills – and share them

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Google is retiring Gemini Gems. Here's what to do to access the same tools as Skills.

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that says “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.)

A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google says. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

#3052. CME vs. Upstart: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

CME's roughly $4 billion profit and near-zero leverage stand in contrast to Upstart's 64% revenue surge, but the lending specialist's leverage and negative free cash flow tell a different story.

By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 7:11AM EST

10 stocks we like better than CME Group ›

Investors today can choose between the massive cash generation of a global financial exchange and the high-growth disruption of an AI lending platform. Is CME Group (CME -1.71%) or Upstart (UPST +1.60%) the better buy?

CME Group provides the critical infrastructure for global risk management, while Upstart uses advanced technology to redefine personal credit. While both companies operate within the financial services sector, they offer very different risk and reward profiles. Comparing their recent performance and valuation can help you decide which stock fits your 2027 goals.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, CME Group describes its position as the world's leading derivatives marketplace. The company provides essential trading and clearing services across major asset classes. Key partnerships include a strategic 10-year cloud infrastructure deal with Alphabet (GOOGL +1.17%) (GOOG +1.23%) and a prediction markets joint venture with Flutter Entertainment (FLUT -0.50%). In 2025, one clearing firm accounted for nearly 12% of total clearing and transaction fees. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each company's latest full fiscal year. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $6.5 billion, representing 6.4% growth over the previous fiscal year. Net income for the period was close to $4 billion. This high level of profitability stems from the company's vital role in global financial markets.

As of CME's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1. This low ratio shows that total debt is only a small fraction of shareholder equity. The current ratio of roughly 1 measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets. Free cash flow was approximately $4.2 billion in fiscal 2025. This metric represents the cash remaining after a business covers its operating expenses and capital expenditures.

Upstart operates an AI-powered lending marketplace that aims to modernize traditional credit scoring. The company connects individual borrowers with more than 100 bank and credit union partners. Its business relies on high-traffic aggregators like Credit Karma to attract new applicants to the platform. This ecosystem currently places the company among the most innovative fintech stocks in the market today.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Upstart reported revenue of approximately $1 billion. This represented a substantial 64% increase compared to the prior 12-month period. The company also returned to profitability, reporting net income of nearly $53.6 million. This turnaround highlights the potential scalability of its AI-driven lending model.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 2.3. This means total liabilities are more than double the company's shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 3, indicating the company has three times more short-term assets than short-term liabilities. Free cash flow for the period was negative $166.1 million.

CME Group faces risks from global market volatility and fluctuations in trading volumes. Its reliance on technology infrastructure makes it susceptible to cybersecurity threats, such as the cooling failure at a CyrusOne data center in late 2025. The company also deals with intense competition from rivals like Intercontinental Exchange (ICE -1.32%) and Cboe Global Markets (CBOE -1.84%). Licensing agreements with benchmark providers such as S&P Global (SPGI -1.67%) also present ongoing intellectual property risks.

Upstart is highly dependent on a limited number of lending partners and institutional investors for loan funding. The company also carries risks if its proprietary AI models contain errors or fail to account for changing macroeconomic conditions. Furthermore, it is currently involved in securities class action lawsuits alleging misrepresentation of its model's effectiveness. Regulatory scrutiny over fair lending compliance and the bank partnership model remains a persistent concern for the business.

CME Group currently trades at a lower forward P/E than Upstart, which suggests it is priced more conservatively relative to future earnings estimates.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

These two companies are in very different stages of the business life cycle. CME Group is a mature, established organization, with roots dating back to the 19th century. Upstart, meanwhile, was founded in 2012 and only went public in late 2020. The derivatives specialist also boasts a strong 60%-plus net margin, while Upstart is only barely profitable.

Upstart's stock has been a disappointment since its public debut. Indeed, it's hovering near 52-week lows. That said, CME Group has lagged the market (though not as badly), trailing the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.00%) by more than 20 percentage points.

These stocks, I think, fundamentally appeal to very different investors. Those interested in innovative companies with skyrocketing revenue and growth potential would probably pick Upstart. Investors who prefer strong margins paired with a modest dividend would likely opt for CME Group. I'm in the latter camp: CME gets my vote for 2027 and beyond.

#3050. Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft announced two new AI models at Ignite 2026 that promise impressive performance for much lower cost. They could reshape its relationship with OpenAI and Anthropic for good.

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two new frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first

A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

There’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

#3047. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

#3046. Hackers Are Using AI to Speed Through Cyberattacks, FBI Warns

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

The agency says the Artex tool is helping attackers target organizations worldwide, including banks, government agencies and healthcare providers.

An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks. The FBI says hackers are using Artex, an AI-powered security testing tool, to break into organizations worldwide. In an advisory on Friday, the agency said some attacks took less than 3 hours from selecting a target to gaining high-level access to its systems. Attackers have used Artex since at least August against banks, government agencies, technology companies and healthcare providers.

The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began. Microsoft attributed its disruption to technical problems, and the FAA says it has found no indication of a cyberattack.

An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.

The warning adds to concerns about the security risks posed by AI agents, which can carry out tasks with little human supervision.

Artex automates security tests that organizations use to uncover weaknesses. According to Microsoft’s analysis, its agents can examine defenses, exploit flaws and extract data. Attackers can use that automation to try several ways into a network simultaneously.

The FBI cited attacks against South Korean financial institutions that exposed the personal information of approximately 67,000 people. Microsoft warns that attackers breached over 2,250 organizations’ Microsoft 365 systems in a separate campaign, using stolen ConnectWise backup credentials alongside the Artex tool.

Because customers had already authorized the backup software, attackers could use its access without logging in as an individual user. Microsoft cautioned that a successful sign-in doesn’t necessarily mean data was accessed or stolen. The automated attacks could trigger security alerts, but their speed left defenders little time to respond.

This FBI Cyber advisory on ARTEX was released last Friday, 11/13. It is not a new announcement, and the FBI has not issued any additional warning since. The guidance in the advisory remains current.We released this advisory last week because as we head to the end of the year,…

Amazon Web Services’ Nov. 13 research described another scheme: Stealing credentials for AI services, and then using that access to hunt for more credentials at someone else’s expense. Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the activity through decoy systems posing as AI services. It linked the campaigns to Artex with moderate confidence but couldn’t independently verify results the agents reported on systems outside its monitoring.

Amazon said the attacks relied on default passwords, exposed login details and outdated software, all of which hackers can find and exploit faster with AI.

Artex’s developer removed the original GitHub repository in October after reports of abuse, but copies remain available, the FBI said. The agency recommends limiting access to sensitive systems, reviewing software permissions, replacing exposed credentials, and monitoring unusual account activity or large data transfers.

In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

#3044. I've Been Wrong About Paypal Stock for 2 Years. Here's Why I'm Finally Changing My Mind.

PayPal raised its 2026 guidance as Venmo and AI-powered commerce gain traction. Here's what could keep the turnaround going, and what could stall it.

By Rick Orford – Nov 18, 2026 at 7:15AM EST

Investors have been skeptical of PayPal (PYPL -0.79%) for the past two years, and for good reason. Specifically, the company has struggled with slowing growth and intensifying competition.

That said, in its third-quarter 2026 results, reported on Oct. 27, PayPal raised its full-year adjusted earnings guidance following its stronger-than-expected performance. On top of that, between Venmo's growth potential and PayPal's push into artificial intelligence (AI)-powered commerce, the company may finally be turning a corner.

Under new CEO Enrique Lores, who took over in March 2026, PayPal is undergoing a broader transformation to simplify operations, improve accountability, and identify new sources of growth.

Instead of relying heavily on its traditional checkout business, management is seeking to derive greater value from its ecosystem, including Venmo, merchant processing, and consumer financial services.

And there are already some encouraging signs. Management highlighted improving momentum across several of its key growth businesses, suggesting that its turnaround efforts are starting to pay off.

Of course, PayPal faces several risks. For example, its branded checkout business remains a concern, with growth of just 1% in the third quarter, highlighting competition from other payment providers. On top of that, the company faces execution risks as it restructures operations and expands consumer financial services.

Overall, although it's still in the early stages, the combination of a more focused strategy and improving execution gives investors a reason to reconsider the company's long-term prospects, especially as it finds new ways to drive growth, starting with Venmo.

Specifically, one of the more interesting parts of PayPal's business is Venmo, which has grown into a broader consumer financial platform. Lately, the company has been expanding Venmo through debit cards, merchant payments, and other financial services. This matters because every additional use case creates another opportunity to generate revenue from an existing customer relationship.

In fact, during the third quarter of 2026, Venmo's payment volume grew 14% year over year, marking its eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and making it one of the company's strongest growth drivers. Further, its Pay with Venmo offering grew by 43%, suggesting consumers are using the platform more for everyday purchases rather than just for money transfers.

Looking ahead, if management can successfully monetize more customer activity on Venmo, the platform could become a meaningful contributor to the company's earnings recovery.

But Venmo isn't the only part of PayPal's ecosystem showing promise.

Meanwhile, PayPal is looking at what could become its next major growth opportunity: AI-powered commerce. After all, even if consumers increasingly discover products through AI platforms, they still need reliable ways to complete purchases.

Plus, payments, identity verification, and security remain important to the shopping experience.

In January 2026, PayPal announced collaborations with Microsoft to power Copilot Checkout and with Alphabet to support Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).

Beyond that, PayPal has been expanding its capabilities through its agreement to acquire Cymbio, a commerce orchestration platform that helps merchants make their products available across AI-driven shopping channels.

Looking ahead, if this new shopping model gains widespread adoption, PayPal could benefit from a new source of payment activity while helping merchants reach customers across multiple digital platforms.

With that, PayPal is pursuing these newer opportunities alongside its broader push to make its existing consumer and merchant businesses more profitable.

Venmo, AI-powered commerce, and a stronger focus on execution give PayPal several opportunities to reignite growth. These days, at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 9.9, PayPal looks discounted, suggesting that investors are pricing in a lot of skepticism around its recovery.

If management can sustain the turnaround and grow earnings consistently, there could be room for a rerating as investor confidence improves, which means the market could pay a higher multiple for each dollar of earnings. That said, the turnaround is far from guaranteed, but for the first time in a while, investors have reasons to be optimistic.

#3043. GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over a decade in the making, GTA 6 is a colossal, polished game with a core love story about the American dream: Doing enough crime to retire early.

The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on.

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.

Environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable. Bystanders and police react more naturally to your presence and culpability — cops now have to see you escaping the crime scene to tag you as a suspect for pursuit. You can talk people down from fights. And the game’s titular transgression of stealing cars is more nuanced than ever.

Granted, early versions of some of these advancements were explored in Rockstar’s interim game, 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, and the series iteratively progressed with all the updates that continue to this day for GTA Online, which was built out from GTA 5 to be an ever-evolving game-as-a-service. But they’ve been taken to the next level in GTA 6, leading to a world that feels more responsive to your presence and actions. With all its systems, map space and activities, it feels like the megayacht of gaming — a polished experience in all its corners, with some of the most detailed graphics you’ll find in gaming.

A lot of that rests on the shoulders of the game’s protagonists, lovers in crime Lucia and Jason, who operate radically differently from previous GTA point-of-view characters. Their romance (if players choose to pursue it) offers a whole new narrative and systematic view of a life outside the law, with collaborative and solo missions that paint a vivid picture of the playful, dangerous world of GTA. Outside story missions, casually driving around as a couple fills the dead air with conversation and the robberies with partnered backup, enriched by their growing relationship, lathering their activities with all the sweetness of a violent date night.

The couple’s story is a very lengthy affair — at 50 hours in, the game says I’ve completed roughly 70% of it — and is robust enough to justify the price of entry. It’s a compelling narrative about two people trying to build a future through a dangerous world by leaning deeper into the danger, but it’s also a showcase of the world Rockstar built. After the story is done, the game hands you the keys to explore it yourself however you’d like.

Rockstar declined to comment on whether GTA 6 will transition into the next version of GTA Online, but it feels like an inevitability. It’s hard to ignore the vast space, systems and mechanics that players only briefly dabble with while playing through the story. From fishing to treasure hunting in underwater shipwrecks to big game hunting to street racing, there’s a lot of low-stakes fodder to unwind with the game — and plenty of bank heists, chases and other random crimes to ratchet up the tension, too.

At launch, GTA 6 has a broad foundation of things to do that — I suspect — will increase over time. It’s layered with Rockstar’s signature puerile humor, and I’ll fess up to laughing at some of the frequent boner jokes and crass names (one sportscar brand is the “pfister”), but the occasional homophobia and transphobia is bizarrely out of time — the game’s mock-everything culture still feels rooted in the 2000s, aimed at people who loved the edginess of South Park in its heyday. More modern satire appears in bystander conversations that range into absurd caricatures of far-right anti-woke crusaders and rabid leftists, but given the game’s faux-Florida setting in the fictional state of Leonida (which includes the legendary Vice City), there’s far more of the former than the latter.

Thus, the world feels textured even for players just picking up the game to fool around. While there are sparse stretches of the map, little side stories unfold for those who notice and follow strange things afoot. But a massive part of the game’s appeal and heart lies in the ballad of two lovebirds, kept apart by immaturity and circumstance but brought together through crime and the skewed American dream at the center of every GTA: Pull off a big enough heist and the world is yours.

The game’s story opens from Jason’s perspective — a twentysomething guy, former military, quiet and gruff, drifting through life doing odd jobs for a small-time kingpin out in the sticks. A little drug-running and skirmishing with the local gangs keep him busy, working out and drinking beers on his deck, watching the sunset from GTA 6’s version of the Florida Keys.

All that changes when Lucia, who stole and then broke his heart, gets out of prison on early release and asks to crash with him during her parole. A tenuous second chance is complicated when she reconnects with a former cellmate who’s partnered with a rich hotshot dangling wealth in front of our fragile couple. This could be the ticket to a financial foundation to help them start anew. Then a job goes wrong, and the pair go on the run, restarting in a rural backwater as far from the clubs of Vice City as one can get.

This is where players decide how close they want Jason and Lucia to be. The game sets up the beginnings of their reconnection, but they can drift apart if players don’t choose to bring them closer. It’s all about the little things: Jason holding the door for Lucia, one of them buying clothes for the other at the vendor, or even just sidling close during morning coffee. Rockstar didn’t want to force players into this relationship — even if things fizzle, the pair will still go through the game as partners in crime, doing jobs together even if they sleep apart.

But players will value something if they have to work for it, Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, told me over a video call. He likened the couple’s relationship to how players embraced the honor system in RDR2, with more taking the high honor route than being a vicious criminal.

“When you can lose something, it’s more meaningful if you work to keep it,” Nelson said.

As Nelson explained, Rockstar came off of GTA 5’s story with its three protagonists wondering how to one-up it for the sequel, which started development soon after in 2015 but took until early 2019 to settle on GTA 6’s main pair. A romantic couple is indeed a step up from characters who come together for a job and split after, and Rockstar had to figure out how that’s different for lovers — they’re not going to end a job at 2 a.m. and part ways; they’re going home to go to bed, Nelson said.

The couple essentially have a run-on conversation that lasts through the story, piping up during long drives to chat about a recent mission or bring up something from their pasts. How much these topics are tailored to events and how much are randomly chosen feels cleverly obscured, coming off like the natural chatter between two people slowly figuring each other out. The sheer scale of the recorded dialogue dwarfs other games and becomes a feature among many, showcasing the titanic work Rockstar put into GTA 6.

It all adds up to a compelling narrative centered on two characters, carefully chiseled to embody the best and worst of Vice City, inspired by the real-life Bonnie and Clyde and by crime couples from films like True Romance and Natural Born Killers. GTA 6’s couple starts with a meet-cute over trying to steal the same car, and freshly out of prison, Lucia eggs on Jason to take bigger illegal jobs than the small-time gigs he’s coasted on. Even with an ankle monitor and picking up road trash on work duty, Lucia never seriously considers staying on the right side of the law. Jason is cautious about new opportunities, but eager not to lose Lucia again, and never considers going straight.

Nestled within their stories is a serious point about the futility of staying honest in a city and system that caters to the rich and punishes the desperate. A flashback shows Lucia juggling gig economy rideshare driving and having her utilities shut off after failed payments, which is heartbreakingly real. But it’s a blip amid the overwhelming focus on a criminal romance, where the only escape from poverty is to steal big bills until finally retiring to a distant island beyond the consequences of your felonious lifestyle.

It’s not surprising — that’s the GTA fantasy, after all — but it’s telling which things Rockstar took great pains to update to modern tastes over the game’s decade-plus development (and what it left out). Smartphones are a huge part of the game’s social interactions, from texting and calling contacts to Instagram-like social media feeds to summoning cars through an app or hailing a ride. But notably absent are any gig economy services that have normalized atypical incomes — you can’t TaskRabbit or Uber your way to an honest living in GTA 6. Odd jobs come as under-the-table favors you do for the rich and powerful, frequently taking advantage of both protagonists’ gray morals.

Though it won’t give you the option of a legal living, GTA 6 leans into the injustice of the wealth gap, putting a few city blocks between gang-riddled run-down apartments and the high-rise clubs populated by ignorant rich assholes. The game gleefully showcases the hypocrisy of the privileged — one time, I rushed into a rural, well-off house where a wife espousing family values ushered me to help her dying husband… who was choking in a BDSM leather harness. Once freed, he tucked his tail back into his submissive role as a “liberal cuck” for their roleplay.

This kind of edginess-for-laughs is peppered around the game, and it’s hard not to feel the cynicism. I can de-escalate some situations, but a lot of the non-player characters you run into on the street are on a hair-trigger eager to fight. You’ll overhear plenty of anti-immigrant screeds from random bystanders. Junkies try to break into your car if you have contraband in the trunk.

If GTA 5 was released in the waning Obama years with waning public optimism, GTA 6 launches halfway into Trump’s second term, where far-right government ICE deportations and street killings have polarized the nation beyond anything we’ve seen in decades. Yet when I asked how Rockstar had adjusted the game over its long development to suit this moment, Nelson said that Jason and Lucia’s story is a counterweight of optimism and care amid all the crime and societal disparity in the game.

“Choosing love is a bit of an act of rebellion against a narcissistic culture,” Nelson said. “The ideas of selfishness and selflessness put through this world is interesting to us, giving you goals other than just maxing out your bank account with supercars and properties.”

Evaluating a game with so much detail spread across a vast map area is difficult, as the polish can be mistaken for quality. When I parked in a narrow driveway, I noticed Jason has an entire animation for shimmying through a slim gap. There have to be a dozen sequences for ways he and Lucia can sidle up to each other for a quick peck or embrace, all optional. There must be a thousand or more buildings you can duck into to explore their interiors. And the amount of dialogue feels unfathomably colossal, all voiced with aplomb by talented actors.

Where other games have some, GTA 6 has more. It’s a little like asking whether a megayacht is enjoyable to commute to work. The simple answer is yes, GTA 6 is an incredible game. And yet, its scope can be distracting. Halfway through the story, I was zipping from destroying drug dens to stealing valuable cars for a collector to hunting big game in the rural hills — all good fun, but my attention easily peeled away from the main story and the couple’s attempt to secure their financial independence, retire early future. The last chapter had ended in a gun battle as hired killers came for a dangerous MacGuffin in Jason and Lucia’s hands, but amid all the good, clean street crime, that danger had receded to the background.

The story’s punch is diluted by everything you can and probably will do, which feels like forgetting the taste of the prime rib after sampling everything else at a buffet. But at least all those activities are enjoyable and round out the criminal with the casual, including mini golf and mud races far from the dense urban core of Vice City. It’s like if Lego Island grew up to add larceny to its roster of fun things to do.

In grappling with the scale of the game, I repeatedly reach for simile — too many options make it harder to fully define GTA 6 and who it’s for, outside of saying there’s so much that its appeal spreads very wide. There’s not quite something for everyone, but it offers such a plethora of side activities that if one gets tiring, another will probably tide you over. This is what will most likely form the foundation of an eventual transition to GTA Online: A substantial stream of things to do on top of stacking cash. And given GTAO’s sustained success, the baseline version of GTA 6 will please all the heist junkies and freeform adventurers who’ve loved the series, even if they aren’t hooked by the well-crafted core story. All the looky-loos curious about the hype will find one of the most polished video games ever made.

GTA fans will notice a lot of small improvements that clean up logical inconsistencies. Witnesses have to notice you doing a crime to report it, and cops have to see you flee a crime scene to put out an all-points bulletin on your description, though you can lower your chances of being recognized by swapping outfits and respraying the color of your getaway ride.

Other new features add complexity to the game. Certain crimes are riskier until you get new tools and connections unlocked through the story, which let you steal cars with trackers and rob banks with countermeasures. Exercise and diet affect your health and physique, which you’ll need to maintain with regular workouts. You can steal guns and vehicles, but they won’t be saved unless you pay to buy or register them, respectively.

These sound tedious, but they’re little frictions that make living in the world of GTA 6 more intentional. Early in the game as Jason, I frequently found myself waking up in the morning, grabbing a cup of coffee and doing a workout to get my in-game day “started,” putting on the radio and feeding my snake or checking in with Lucia ambling around the kitchen. As the relationship between the two deepens, they can go to bed together, cuddled up and doomscrolling on their phones.

While I expect a million posts of “he just like me fr fr” to blanket social media as people wonder at the work Rockstar put in to replicate our (often terrible) habits, there’s still a lot I was delighted to discover that’s unique to the world they’ve made. Some of these are jokes taken to an extreme, like the intentionally pretentious game-within-a-game you can play, Tenebrae Lux — a black-and-white walking simulator by an in-universe auteur, Johannes Zuch, whose name flashes on the screen so many times that it feels like a wink toward Hideo Kojima and other famous game creators.

“We love auteurs — it’s not mocking, it’s celebrating,” Nelson said.

But my favorite things in any GTA game are the side stories you can chance upon that are scripted but feel emergent, exploring the bizarre nooks and crannies of the world. One night halfway through the game, I was casually driving around as Lucia when I saw a police chopper aiming a spotlight at the street — and found the cops in a standoff with a man in a fox suit.

I immediately discovered that, in the game’s fictional state of Leonida, being a furry (e.g., wearing a fursuit and expressing your fursona) is illegal, so I broke through the police blockade to liberate him. I met up with his fellow furries and spirited them away to a compound, during which I peeked over my shoulder to find them nuzzling each other. God bless you little oddballs bravely living your truth in the face of unjust laws.

Like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple, and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned.

Eventually, you’ll face that ultimate temptation to cause such havoc that you’ll trigger the game’s new, sixth star of police attention — one in which it feels like every cop in Leonida is coming after you, and it doesn’t stop until you’re arrested or put down, a countdown to how long Jason and Lucia can stick it to the law at maximum volume.

“I haven’t played six stars since we finalized it, I made it too long so we made it harder,” Nelson said. “I’m curious to see what times people get!”

#3042. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#3041. A Recession Could Be Coming, and History Says This 1 Investing Move Has Never Once Failed

This one thing has happened after every bear market in history.

By David Dierking – Nov 18, 2026 at 7:30AM EST

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›

Recession headlines tend to trigger very emotional responses from investors. They often suggest the worst is coming and give the impression that you have to do something now or risk losing even more money.

While that feeling is understandable, studies have shown that doing nothing actually produces some of the best results. A recent DALBAR study found that the average investor in both equity and fixed income funds over a two-decade period significantly trailed their index benchmarks.

The reason usually cited for this is over-trading and market timing. Investors often sell after losses have already occurred and don't buy back until the recovery is already in progress. As a result, they miss out on performance gains.

Here's why long-term buy-and-hold is the one strategy that succeeds over and over.

The U.S. economy has gone through numerous recessions, generational economic crises, and bear markets over the past century. The stock market has fallen sharply in nearly all of them. Yet every time in history, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.06%) has recovered and reached a new all-time high.

That's the big difference between short-term volatility and long-term growth. The U.S. economy is cyclical. It'll go through periods of expansion and contraction, and of asset prices rising and falling. That's a normal part of investing in assets that come with risk, and it should be expected.

But the long-term trajectory of the U.S. economy has been up. Gross domestic product, the number of people employed, household incomes, and corporate earnings have all continued to rise over time. Those are the factors that matter most. When investing for the long term, you should focus on these decades-long uptrends, not the short-term ups and downs that occur along the way. The only way to capture those uptrends is to stay invested throughout these cycles.

That doesn't just mean that investors can or should put their money in anything. The core of any equity portfolio should be built around durable, high-quality companies that can withstand a range of market and economic environments. Some of the more speculative or emerging companies could go bankrupt in their first adverse economic environment. But the big, quality companies with healthy balance sheets should be able to survive economically weak periods.

But one of the only ways to consistently take advantage of these characteristics is to stay invested. Let the long-term compounding of growth do the work for you.

#3040. Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Almost Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You don't have to delete old games to make space for GTA 6 if you don't want to. Here are your other options.

The wait is almost over. Grand Theft Auto 6 hits shelves tomorrow, Nov. 19, and if you preordered the game, you can preload it on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S now. Preloading ensures you can quickly boot the game up when it’s released.

Rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have two options: delete games or upgrade your console’s hard drive. Here’s what you should know about both options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 will be available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to purchase either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, won’t get the highest visual quality and will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

You only have a few days left until Rockstar releases GTA 6, so you’d better prepare your digital storage now, or you might not be immediately able to play. I plan on deleting old games to make room on my console. You won’t catch me slipping on Nov. 19.

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

With the repository added, you can install it with:

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. #3037. Disney Imagineers Have Built AI-Powered ‘Star Wars’ Alien Audio-Animatronics With AWS

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Semi-exclusive: Three original Anzellan characters with distinct personalities will interact with guests in Disney parks.

Disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland. But today, new robotic characters are being powered up with artificial intelligence.

In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three new Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

Anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe. They include Babu Frik in Star Wars: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker and the droidsmiths introduced in season 3 of The Mandalorian. The droidsmiths take on larger roles in The Mandalorian and Grogu, helping Baby Yoda rescue Din Djarin from the Hutts.

The new Anzellan animatronics built by Disney Imagineers use AWS cloud and AI capabilities in order to “understand the scene around them,” Kyle Laughlin, SVP of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, tells me.

“If you imagine walking into an experiential retail store, you now will be greeted not by a pre-scripted animation or interaction, but a totally personalized experience where each of these Anzellans [has] their own personalities,” Laughlin says, adding that they’ll be attuned to “how many people are in the room, the ages of people, the general size and type of guest.”

The animatronic aliens will be able to interact with guests, right down to commenting on people who are wearing a birthday button or even a certain Star Wars T-shirt. Speaking with these animatronics will give guests the same experience they would have when meeting a character walking around the park, Laughlin adds. They also play off each other and react to what each other are doing, with no one controlling them behind the scenes.

The three audio-animatronic prototypes, which will make their first appearance during AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas on Nov. 30 before moving into one of the Disney Parks, are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a.

They’re original characters created just for this project in partnership with Lucasfilm and the filmmakers, and they all have their own personalities devised by the Imagineers. Vilo is the boss, Kado is the droidsmith mechanic who wants to be the center of attention and Jibu, though Kado’s twin, is the shy one. The animatronics speak a mix of English (or Galactic Basic in-universe) and Anzellan, as they do in the Star Wars movies and TV series, and have hundreds of thousands of prerecorded lines of dialogue to draw from when talking to guests and each other.

Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising and Sports, tells me this is “one of the most delightful examples” of physical AI.

“When you talk about physical AI, it’s AI that perceives, it reasons and it acts in the real world,” she says. “It’s not just AI on a screen.”

Bakhtiar says Disney was able to use both AWS cloud computing and AI tools to “get from idea to implementation several magnitudes faster than they would have otherwise,” with Laughlin specifying it took “mere months.”

Imagineers used an AWS coding agent called Kiro that built their creative briefs into software, which was then reviewed by humans. Imagineers also used the Amazon Bedrock fully managed AI service, which allows them to choose between all the biggest AI models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

“We’re providing Amazon Bedrock to the Imagineering team to be able to leverage the right models that they need at the right time to be able to really enhance those character experiences,” Bakhtiar tells me. “From multimodal models that focus on voice to world models, to large language models. The point is that they are able to get the right tool at the right time and then do so in a way that’s secure, resilient, performant and globally available.”

Bakhtiar says AWS is continuing to work with Disney, though the next project is under wraps.

“The future of entertainment is going to be highly personalized,” she says. “It’s going to be multidimensional, and it’s going to be more interactive than ever. And I think this is an incredible example of that coming to life.”

Disney had previously teamed up with Nvidia on robotics and AI to bring a robot version of fan-favorite Frozen character Olaf to life so he can wander around Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland, and is also now exploring robots paired with AI that could guide guests throughout Disneyland parking lots.

“You can imagine an entire franchise of characters working and interacting with one another,” says Laughlin. “We’ve done a number of things in the Star Wars universe. We’re just getting started in Frozen, and we have a wealth of IP that we can mine to bring those characters to our guests as fast as possible.”
